items.title: Jules Cahn Interview, 1974-10-06
items.q: No direct interaction or personal relationship described between the interviewee and James Sugarbar Crawford in the provided text.

ctx.x: The words seem to have meaning, and they are, a lot of it is a sort of a pidgin English, and you listen real closely and listen and listen and listen. And you'll be able to pick out a number of phrases. But still there are a number that I've been unable to, to really pick out. You'll hear them say, here come a gang. Let me hear from the spy boy and so forth. But there's still a lot that I don't understand. Like Two Way Park Away, which is, I really don't know what it means. I think it's a derivative of get out of…

We're going to listen to that a little while later. But first, this is a song that was done in 1954 by another New Orleans artist, who again I think was influenced by the Indians, James Sugarbar Crawford. And the song was called Ico Ico. Ico.
